meta.title: Portolan: An opinionated standard for cloud-native geospatial catalogs
meta.description: Portolan publishes geospatial data as plain files on object storage, with no servers, no databases, and no proprietary licenses. Structured metadata lets a person or an agent read a catalog and query it directly. The standard sets the quality bar, a validator enforces it, tools make catalogs cheap to build, and a registry connects them into a network anyone can search.

hero.title: Portolan makes geospatial data
hero.description: Portolan combines cloud-native file formats with clear metadata and documentation so that people and agents can publish and use data at any scale. This makes data easier to find, understand, and analyze in new ways.

open.title: Open and interoperable
open.description: Portolan builds on existing OGC-compliant formats like <m>GeoParquet</m>, <m>COG</m>, and <m>STAC</m> so that data can be dropped right into tools like QGIS, ArcGIS, Pandas, or BigQuery with no disruptions or difficulties.

simple.title: Simple, cheap, scalable, sovereign
simple.description: A Portolan catalog lives in your cloud storage and requires no servers, databases, or APIs. It works with any <m>S3</m>-compatible cloud provider in any location, whether you use AWS or Azure, Hetzner or MinIO, and scales from megabytes to petabytes. Your only costs are what you pay your cloud provider.

agents.title: Built for people and agents
agents.description: Portolan catalogs are well-structured, well-formatted, and well-documented, so people and agents can find, understand, and use them. Browse the registry yourself to discover new data, or point an agent at the registry and see what it can find and do.

large.title: Large publishers
large.today: Large archives, such as satellite imagery or national-scale geoportals, are expensive to store and hard to maintain.
large.change: Portolan makes it straightforward to publish that data <cost>as cheaply as possible</cost>, without servers, databases, or APIs, while making it easier to discover and use.

small.title: Small publishers
small.today: Many city governments, NGOs, and other smaller data producers can't afford the cost or complexity of publishing data with tools like GeoServer or Esri.
small.change: Portolan lowers the barrier to entry by letting you share your data with nothing more than a cloud storage bucket.

users.title: Data users
users.today: Most geospatial data is scattered, poorly documented, and stored in ways that make it hard to use.
users.change: Portolan requires clear metadata and documentation, uses formats designed for direct access, and provides a <reg>central registry</reg> of public catalogs. You spend less time finding, downloading, and wrangling data, and more time putting it to work.

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.intro: Use the <cli>Portolan CLI</cli> or <skills>agent skills</skills> to transform your existing data into a Portolan catalog.
howItWorks.figAlt: Existing files and services flow into portolan-cli, which pushes a catalog to object storage. QGIS, Python, and agents read it directly.

convert.title: Convert
convert.description: Your existing data are converted to cloud-native formats. Whether you're working with Shapefiles and GeoPackages, a WFS endpoint, or an Esri server, you'll end up with <m>GeoParquet</m> for vector and <m>COG</m> for raster.

catalog.title: Catalog
catalog.description: Your cloud-optimized data are organized as a <m>STAC</m> catalog with clear metadata and docs, including READMEs and <m>AGENTS.md</m>. This makes the catalog easy to find, explore, and use, for both people and agents.

publish.title: Publish
publish.description: Your catalog is published to any S3-compatible storage, like AWS, GCS, Hetzner, or MinIO. There are no servers or APIs to set up. Sharing it means sending someone the URL.

use.title: Use
use.description: The data can now be used directly in tools like QGIS, ArcGIS, or Python, or you can pass the catalog URL to an agent and let it get to work with the Portolan consume skill.
